questions.q: What is the main role of the Creative Cloud desktop app?
options: A design tool for editing photos
The launcher, updater and sync client for your Adobe apps and assets
questions.explain: The desktop app is not a design tool itself; it installs and updates apps and syncs your assets.

questions.q: Where do you toggle automatic updates for your Adobe apps?
options: Creative Cloud desktop app menu > Preferences > Apps > Auto-update
questions.explain: Open the desktop app's menu, go to Preferences > Apps and switch on Auto-update.

questions.q: What does a Creative Cloud Library hold?
options: Reusable assets such as colors, character styles, graphics and images that sync across apps
Backups of whole Photoshop documents only
Only fonts installed on your machine
questions.explain: Libraries are containers of reusable assets that sync to Adobe's servers and appear in every app you sign into.

questions.q: A menu item from a lesson isn't where described in your version. What does the lesson suggest?
options: Check Help > About for your version and search the in-app Help bar for the command name
questions.explain: Panel positions can shift between versions; the command usually still exists, just relocated.

questions.q: Photoshop is best described as which kind of editor?
questions.explain: Photoshop works on grids of colored pixels, which suits photos and painted artwork.

questions.q: A panel you need has disappeared from the workspace. Where can you restore it?
options: The Window menu, e.g. Window > Layers
questions.explain: Every panel lives under the Window menu and can be toggled back on from there.

questions.q: What is the difference between Opacity and Fill on a layer?
options: Opacity fades the whole layer including layer styles; Fill fades only the layer's own pixels
Opacity only works on text layers
questions.explain: Fill leaves layer styles such as a drop shadow at full strength, which is useful for shadow-only or stroke-only effects.

questions.q: How do you group several selected layers?
options: Hide them with the eye icon
questions.explain: Groups act like folders and keep complex files navigable.

questions.q: Why can vector artwork scale from a business card to a billboard without losing sharpness?
options: It is stored as a very large pixel grid
It is stored as mathematical paths of points and curves
questions.explain: Vector shapes are paths defined mathematically, so they render crisply at any size.

questions.q: What can a single Illustrator document hold that Photoshop documents cannot in the same way?
questions.explain: One file can contain many artboards, such as a logo at three sizes.

questions.q: Which tool selects and drags individual anchor points within a shape?
questions.explain: The Selection tool moves whole shapes; Direct Selection edits individual anchor points and segments.

questions.q: What does holding Shift while dragging the Rectangle or Ellipse tool do?
options: Constrains the shape to a perfect square or circle
questions.explain: Shift constrains proportions so rectangles become squares and ellipses become circles.

questions.q: What does the Source Monitor show?
options: The sequence as it will play
A clip before it is placed on the timeline, where you can set in/out points
questions.explain: The Program Monitor previews the sequence; the Source Monitor previews raw clips.

questions.q: A clip shows a red offline warning after you moved the source file. What fixes it?
options: Right-click the clip and choose Link Media
questions.explain: Imported clips are references to files on disk, so a moved file must be relinked.

questions.q: Which tool cuts a clip into two at the point you click?
questions.explain: The Razor tool splits a clip so each part can be moved or deleted independently.

questions.q: What does Ripple Delete (Shift+Delete) do?
options: Removes a segment but leaves a gap
Removes a segment and closes the gap it leaves
questions.explain: Ripple Delete removes the selected segment and shifts later clips to close the gap.

questions.q: What is a composition in After Effects?
options: Its unit of work, similar to a Premiere sequence but built for layering and animating
questions.explain: A composition (comp) is where layers are stacked and animated.

questions.q: Which shortcut reveals a selected layer's Opacity property?
questions.explain: P is Position, S Scale, R Rotation and T Opacity.

questions.q: You set one keyframe on a property and nothing else. What happens?
options: It sets a fixed value with no motion
After Effects adds a second keyframe
questions.explain: You need at least two keyframes at different times with different values for any animation.

questions.q: How do you enable keyframing on a property?
options: Click the stopwatch icon next to the property name
questions.explain: Clicking the stopwatch turns on keyframing and places the first keyframe at the current time and value.

questions.q: On a layer mask, what does painting with black do?
options: Hides that part of the layer without deleting pixels
questions.explain: Black hides, white reveals and gray partially hides, all non-destructively.

questions.q: You already have an active selection. What does clicking Add Layer Mask do?
options: Converts the selection into a mask, hiding everything outside it
questions.explain: The selection becomes the mask, so everything outside it is hidden immediately.

questions.q: An adjustment layer affects which layers?
options: All layers in the document regardless of order
Layers below it in the stack
questions.explain: Adjustment layers apply to everything beneath them unless clipped to the single layer directly below.

questions.q: How can you limit an adjustment layer to only the single layer directly beneath it?
questions.explain: The clipping mask (Alt/Option+Cmd/Ctrl+G) restricts the adjustment to that one layer.

questions.q: Which Pathfinder operation cuts the topmost shape out of the shapes below it?
questions.explain: Minus Front subtracts the front shape, as when making a crescent from two circles.

questions.q: Which Pathfinder operation keeps only the area where the selected shapes overlap?
questions.explain: Intersect keeps the overlap, such as the lens shape of a Venn diagram.

questions.q: Where do you open the Pathfinder panel?
questions.explain: Window > Pathfinder (Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+F9) opens it.

questions.q: After a Pathfinder operation, what is the result and how can you refine it?
options: Several linked shapes that cannot be edited
A single new path, refined with the Direct Selection tool
questions.explain: The result is one new path whose points you can adjust with the Direct Selection tool (A).

questions.q: A Cross Dissolve shows a red warning triangle. What is the likely cause and fix?
options: The audio is clipping; lower the volume
The workspace is corrupt; reset it
The project is too long; delete the sequence
The clip has no spare frames beyond the cut; trim less tightly or shorten the transition
questions.explain: A dissolve needs extra frames (trim handles) on both clips to overlap into.

questions.q: What does the Auto-Match button in Essential Sound's Loudness section do?
options: Analyzes the clip and adjusts it toward a target loudness
questions.explain: It is a fast first pass for clips with inconsistent recording levels.

questions.q: Roughly where should dialogue generally peak, per the lesson?
questions.explain: Dialogue should peak around -12 to -6 dB, never slamming into 0 dB, which causes clipping or distortion.

questions.q: When is a dissolve the lesson's recommended choice over a hard cut?
options: Mainly at scene changes or time/location jumps
questions.explain: Use transitions sparingly; a hard cut is still right most of the time.

questions.q: Why is a shared Library better than pasting hex codes into each app?
options: It removes the need for colors
It is a live reference, so one update keeps everything in sync
questions.explain: Manual copies drift when a color changes or a typo creeps in; a Library is one source of truth.

questions.q: How do you save formatted text as a reusable Character Style in the Libraries panel?
options: Drag it into the Project panel
Select the text and click the + (Text) button at the bottom of the panel
questions.explain: The asset stores font, size, tracking and color so it can be applied in one click.

questions.q: Where do Library colors appear in Premiere Pro, per the lesson?
options: In the Essential Graphics panel when editing a graphic or text fill color
questions.explain: Availability can vary by version; if missing, apply the same hex value manually.

questions.q: What is a good practice when adding swatches to a Library?
options: Keep default names like Untitled Color 1
Give meaningful names such as Brand Primary
questions.explain: Meaningful names make shared assets easy to find and apply consistently.

questions.q: Which three connected deliverables does the Brand Kit capstone build?
options: A logo, a poster and a short promo video
A font, a photo and a plugin
A website, an app and a database
A podcast, a book and a slide deck
questions.explain: All three share colors, logo and typography through one Creative Cloud Library.

questions.q: What ties the three deliverables together?
questions.explain: Colors, logo and type come from the shared Library so the pieces stay consistent.

questions.q: In which app is the logo designed?
questions.explain: The logo is designed in Illustrator and saved as a Graphic asset in the Library.

questions.q: Which Level 1 modules does the capstone draw on?
options: Libraries, Illustrator, Photoshop and Premiere Pro work
questions.explain: It combines Libraries (Modules 1 and 9), Illustrator, Photoshop and Premiere Pro editing.

questions.q: Why does scaling a Smart Object repeatedly not accumulate blur?
options: Free Transform scales from the original embedded or linked data, not the last-resampled pixels
questions.explain: The transform is stored as an editable instruction on the container rather than baked into pixels.

questions.q: What is the difference between Place Embedded and Place Linked?
options: Linked stores a copy; Embedded references the file
Embedded stores a full copy inside the .psd; Linked references the external file, keeping the .psd smaller
questions.explain: Linked files stay smaller but depend on the external file remaining in place.

questions.q: What does Replace Contents do on a Smart Object?
options: Swaps the source file while keeping existing transforms, filters and position
questions.explain: It is handy for swapping a placeholder photo for a final one late in a layout.

questions.q: What happens to a filter applied to a Smart Object layer?
options: It is applied to every layer
It becomes an editable Smart Filter with its own mask
questions.explain: You can reopen its settings or paint on its mask to limit where it applies.

questions.q: Which Curves shape is the classic contrast boost?
options: An S-curve: shadows pulled slightly down, highlights pulled slightly up
questions.explain: An S-curve deepens blacks and brightens whites while leaving midtones roughly alone.

questions.q: How can you remove a blue tint from dark areas using Curves?
options: Pull the Blue channel curve down in the shadows
questions.explain: Switching to the Blue channel lets you correct the cast without changing overall brightness.

questions.q: A photo shot under tungsten light looks too orange. What does the lesson suggest in Color Balance?
options: Select Midtones and move Yellow–Blue toward Blue and Cyan–Red slightly toward Cyan
Set Preserve Luminosity off and brighten
questions.explain: Shifting midtones toward the missing colors neutralizes the cast.

questions.q: Why usually leave Preserve Luminosity checked in Color Balance?
options: So a color fix doesn't also brighten or darken the image
questions.explain: It keeps overall brightness unchanged while only shifting color.

questions.q: What do Standard Ligatures do?
options: Join colliding letter pairs such as fi and fl into a single better-fitted glyph
Add decorative script swashes to every letter
questions.explain: Standard ligatures fix pairs that collide at their default spacing.

questions.q: How do Old Style figures differ from Lining figures?
options: Old Style are only for tables
Old Style numerals vary in height and blend quietly into text; Lining numerals are all cap-height
Old Style are all caps height; Lining vary
questions.explain: Lining figures suit all-caps headlines and aligned number tables.

questions.q: What can a Paragraph Style do that a Character Style cannot on its own?
options: Set indents, spacing, alignment and hyphenation for whole paragraphs, and reference a Character Style
questions.explain: One click sets both paragraph settings and the referenced character formatting.

questions.q: Why might most of the OpenType panel be grayed out?
options: The font itself doesn't support those features
questions.explain: OpenType features are built into the font file, and small system fonts often lack them.
